name: PR-Bubble-Cursor
summary: In handheld AR, a 3D bubble is placed with a touch and adjusted in depth and size by swipes; the objects inside appear as 2D clones and the target is tapped among them.
howItWorks: Touching places the bubble; swiping up or down changes its depth and left or right its size. The candidates inside it are shown as flat clones near the cursor and a tap on a clone selects. It had the lowest error rate (0.25%) and was the most preferred. On an iPhone 6 with 12 participants (targets 0.2–1 cm, 20–80% occluded), error rates were 0.25% for PR-Bubble-Cursor, 1.2% for PR-Cone-Casting, 2.7% for touch Go-Go, 4.4% for 2D-Grid-Cursor, 5% for Offset-Ray-Casting and 41% for touch raycasting; times were 0.44 s for raycasting, 0.68 s PR-Cone, 1.22 s Offset, 1.29 s PR-Bubble, 2.06 s Grid and 2.75 s Go-Go. PR-Bubble-Cursor was preferred.

relationships.note: Compared with a touch version of Go-Go where a swipe sets arm length.
